notes.reason: The claim is his own and the note is right. He says 'It ceases to be mentioned in Erskine May I think beyond the 12th edition', and I checked both cited sections of the current online Erskine May, which is the 25th edition of 2019. Paragraph 9.10 'Addresses to the Crown' says 'Usually, the motion for an Address is made in the form "That an humble Address be presented to Her Majesty to ..."', and paragraph 7.31 says 'Returns may be called for by an Order or an humble Address, and it is not always clear which is appropriate.' Both accepted quotes are verbatim and the humble address is plainly still covered. What gives me pause is how little the point carries. The video is about Starmer's position and who succeeds him, and the humble address only comes up as a short aside explaining a procedure Angela Rayner used; nothing in his argument depends on which edition of Erskine May last described it, and his surrounding points that the procedure was popular in the nineteenth century, fell out of use and forces the government to produce papers are all sound. He also flagged the claim as a guess with 'I think', which the note does not acknowledge. He is a former Leader of the House who enjoys procedural detail and the point is apolitical, so he would probably take it in good part, but Nathan should decide whether a correction this small is worth sending.
